recap_lines: The verb of a claim must match the evidence behind it.
A verb downgrade keeps the facts and lowers the posture.
Name the uncertainty, epistemic or aleatoric, and what would change it.
Calibration means the stated chance matches how often the model is right.
Report ECE with its bin count, with MCE and subgroup ECE beside it.
A fix fitted on one population can fail under distribution shift.
bookends.segment: Name The Term, Rule Out The Look-Alike
bookends.command: Quiz me on communicating uncertainty. Give me one short case at a time. For each case I must name the exact term and say why its look-alike is wrong. Use these terms, observe, find, conclude, verb downgrade, epistemic uncertainty, aleatoric uncertainty, calibration, ECE, MCE and distribution shift. Do not show the answer until I reply, then correct me in one sentence.
checks: Check: each case came alone, and the answer waited for your reply.
Check: every correction named the exact term and its look-alike.

beats.narration_text: A ladder of claim verbs, strongest at the top, beside one result written with three verbs. Warranted assertion means your claim may be only as strong as your evidence. Eighty-seven percent on one held-out set supports observe. Find and conclude claim more. For example, a job seeker rewrites their résumé and then gets an interview call. The evidence warrants saying the call came after the rewrite, not that the rewrite caused it.

beats.narration_text: A checklist of what conclude needs. Conclude says the question behind the work is closed. That takes full analysis, alternatives named and rejected, sensitivity analysis, and a finding that survives it. Suggest only says the data are consistent. Few claims warrant it. For example, to conclude that a résumé-tailoring agent raises interview rates, you must rule out rivals, such as a busier hiring season, and check that the result survives sensitivity analysis. Short of that, use a weaker verb, such as suggest.

beats.narration_text: Two boxes share the verb ladder. This is build and audit. Build is your own report, where you match each verb to its proof. Audit is an AI claim handed to you, where you lower the verbs that overreach. One supervisory skill, not two. For example, you build when you write up your own job-search agent and tie each verb to a test. You audit when an AI summary says a tool is proven to win more interviews, and you lower that verb to fit.

beats.narration_text: Four red bars show the interval around an accuracy of zero point eight seven, in this made-up example. Epistemic uncertainty comes from not knowing enough yet, so more evidence shrinks it. From fifty cases to three thousand two hundred, the bar narrows. For example, a model that predicts who gets an interview has been checked on only a small batch of applications. Much of its uncertainty is epistemic, and checking it on many more would narrow it.
